decision.trend: Research has been focused on improving the properties of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) through various processing techniques and compositional modifications. Earlier studies have explored the effects of mechanical alloying, spark plasma sintering, and selective laser melting on the microstructure and properties of HEAs. Recent studies have investigated the use of laser powder bed fusion and high-pressure high-temperature treatment to enhance the strength and ductility of HEAs. The trend suggests a shift towards more advanced processing techniques and a greater emphasis on understanding the relationships between processing, microstructure, and properties.
decision.unsolved: Despite significant progress, the strength-ductility trade-off in HEAs remains a challenge. Many HEAs exhibit high strength but limited ductility, which hinders their potential applications. Further research is needed to develop processing strategies and compositional designs that can overcome this trade-off and achieve a balance between strength and ductility.
decision.why: The next step could involve exploring the effects of doping HEAs with magnetocaloric elements, such as Gd or Dy, to enhance their magnetocaloric properties. This approach has shown promise in other studies, and the unique properties of HEAs make them an attractive platform for developing advanced magnetocaloric materials. By introducing magnetocaloric elements into the HEA composition, researchers may be able to tailor the magnetic properties and achieve improved magnetocaloric performance.
